source_name: CBCG — Usluge kreditnog registra (credit register services)
why_relevant: Describes the CBCG credit register (kreditni registar) — its scope, reporting obligations and services. Useful for understanding what data banks must submit (a driver of reporting/RegTech demand) even though record-level data is restricted.

source_name: CBCG — Godišnji izvještaj o radu (Central Bank annual activity report)
why_relevant: Contains an annual chapter on consumer/user protection with complaint counts, supervisory measures and sanctions against banks, plus payments-infrastructure milestones (e.g. SEPA accession). Stable, machine-readable PDF series.

source_name: Zakon o računovodstvu Crne Gore (Sl. list CG 84/2025) — legal basis for filing & publication
why_relevant: Sets who must file, deadlines (statements to the tax authority by 31 March), audit thresholds and applicable standards. New law published 31 Jul 2025, in force 8 Aug 2025 — a live change that may alter filing scope/format for 2025 accounts.

source_name: Pravilnik o sadržini i formi obrazaca finansijskih iskaza (Sl. list CG 011/20)
why_relevant: Defines the exact schema (bilans stanja / bilans uspjeha / iskaz o novčanim tokovima) of every filed ME annual account. Essential to build a stable parser and to map ME line items to comparable metrics.

source_name: Local media relay of supranational assessments (CdM, Standard, Mondo, Vijesti, ETV) — sr-language early signal
why_relevant: Montenegrin outlets frequently publish draft EC report assessments and MONEYVAL outcomes days before official publication, and enumerate the specific measures/recommendations by chapter. Useful as a leading indicator and for local terminology, but must be corroborated against the primary document.

source_name: Akcioni plan za ispunjenje završnih mjerila u poglavlju 8 – Konkurencija (EU accession Chapter 8 action plan)
why_relevant: EU accession benchmarking documents candidly assess AZZK's enforcement capacity, case throughput and known weaknesses — the calibration needed to know how much absence of decisions means absence of problems versus absence of capacity.

entity_name: Komisija za tržište kapitala Crne Gore
source_name: KTK — Godišnji izvještaj o stanju na tržištu kapitala
why_relevant: Annual regulator report on the state of the Montenegrin capital market: issuer counts, turnover, new issues, enforcement, and a structural view of who is listed. Best single retrospective baseline document for the cell and a pointer to issuers we may have missed.

entity_name: World Bank Open Knowledge Repository / Documents & Reports
source_name: World Bank – Montenegro FSAP Technical Note on Financial Infrastructure (payments and settlement systems)
why_relevant: Rare, granular independent assessment of Montenegro's national payment system (RTGS/DNS), oversight arrangements, credit registry and collateral registry — the structural baseline against which later SEPA/TIPS/instant-payments moves should be read.

entity_name: World Bank Open Knowledge Repository / Documents & Reports
source_name: World Bank – Montenegro Systematic Country Diagnostic (and SCD Update)
why_relevant: Identifies structural constraints including banking-sector vulnerabilities, limits of the central bank's lender-of-last-resort function under euroisation, and credit-market frictions — framing that shapes subsequent lending operations and reform dialogue.

entity_name: World Bank Open Knowledge Repository / Documents & Reports
source_name: World Bank — Montenegro Financial Infrastructure Modernization / SEPA alignment (TIPS Clone) project docs
why_relevant: Financier of ME's payment infrastructure modernization (EUR 8m). Project appraisal documents contain baseline/target indicators, cost structures and timelines rarely disclosed elsewhere — high-value quantitative roadmap evidence.

source_name: EBRD project summary documents & news — Montenegro financial institutions portfolio
why_relevant: EBRD PSDs and press releases name the Montenegrin counterparty bank, facility size and product type (e.g. NLB Banka AD Podgorica EUR 18m package, CKB portfolio risk-sharing, Alter Modus MSME lines). These reveal which banks are recapitalising/expanding and therefore likely to buy channel and payment technology — leading indicators ahead of any tender.

source_name: EBRD – Montenegro Country Strategy (2021-2026 and draft 2026-2031)
why_relevant: Country strategies contain an explicit financial-sector diagnostic (bank concentration, SME finance gap, capital-market depth, digitalisation) and set out the EBRD's planned interventions — a forward view of where donor money and technical assistance will hit Montenegrin banks.

source_name: EBRD Transition Report – Montenegro country assessment (annual)
why_relevant: Annual two-to-four page country assessment with transition-quality scores including a 'competitive/resilient' financial-sector dimension, plus a short list of the year's key financial-sector policy developments. Comparable across Western Balkan peers.

source_name: ICT Cortex — Montenegrin ICT cluster (fintech commentary)
why_relevant: Industry cluster of ME tech companies publishing analysis on PSD2 alignment, instant payments and request-to-pay for POS/e-commerce. Useful for identifying local technology vendors adjacent to payment institutions and processors, and for early reads on domestic rail roadmaps.

source_name: IMF – Montenegro mission concluding statements and Executive Board press releases
why_relevant: Concluding statements appear weeks-to-months before the full staff report and already contain the substantive banking-supervision and AML messages; the Board press release adds the official assessment. Best early-warning channel in this cell.

source_name: IMF – Montenegro Article IV Consultation staff reports (Country Report series)
why_relevant: Annual, deeply quantitative assessment of Montenegro's banking system: capital, liquidity, asset quality, cash-loan and real-estate credit dynamics, macroprudential measures, plus a statistical annex with financial soundness indicators. Also flags payment-system integration (SEPA, TIPS Clone).

source_name: MINA Business — Montenegrin business newswire (payments coverage)
why_relevant: National agency wire that reports CBCG payment-card statistics releases and PSP announcements in local language (e.g. quarterly card-transaction growth figures). Fastest surfacing of numbers that otherwise sit inside CBCG spreadsheets, and picks up PSP press releases with no other distribution.

source_name: MONSTAT Statistički biznis registar (SBR) — methodology and outputs
why_relevant: Documents how MONSTAT builds its business register from administrative sources (CRPS, tax administration), including stratification by activity and size. Tells you exactly which administrative datasets exist behind the scenes and how complete/current they are — a key pointer for feasibility of entity-level coverage.

source_name: MONSTAT Statistical Yearbook / Statistički godišnjak
why_relevant: Annual consolidated volume including finance chapters and data sourced from other official producers (CBCG, ministries). Convenient stable-URL time series for sector aggregates and enterprise counts by activity.

source_name: CFO Asocijacija Crne Gore (Association of Financial Directors)
why_relevant: Newly founded cross-sector CFO association whose membership explicitly spans banking, insurance, telecoms and ICT. Once it has its own site it will be a direct pointer source; for now trade-press coverage is the only located record of its formation and membership.

entity_name: EEAS / Delegation of the EU to Montenegro
source_name: EEAS / EU Delegation to Montenegro — SEPA accession communications
why_relevant: Official EU-side communication on Montenegro becoming operationally part of SEPA — a structural change that resets cross-border euro payment pricing and opens the market to EU-licensed PSPs. Anchors the timeline for rail changes affecting every actor in this cell.

source_name: Borba.me — economic/finance desk (payments policy coverage)
why_relevant: Local outlet that obtains Ministry of Finance statements on payment-market openings (e.g. joint ME–North Macedonia negotiations with PayPal on receiving funds). Reveals prospective rail entrants and policy blockers before any register entry exists.

source_name: European Commission – Montenegro 2025 Report SWD(2025) 754 final (annual progress report PDF)
why_relevant: The single most benchmark-dense annual document on Montenegrin banking/payments alignment: Chapter 9 financial services, Chapter 4 capital movement/payment services, AML, deposit guarantee scheme, SEPA/TIPS-Clone commitments, plus forward-looking recommendations for the next 12 months.

source_name: European Payments Council — news/press on Montenegro SEPA scope
why_relevant: Scheme-owner communications defining ME's geographical-scope inclusion, operational readiness dates and scheme-country list versions (EPC409-09).

source_name: MONSTAT — published procurement decisions (odluka o izboru) and Zakon o javnim nabavkama text (Paragraf.me)
why_relevant: Consolidated legal text of the Law on Public Procurement defines which documents must be published, when, and in what form (plan, tender notice, odluka o izboru, ugovor, izvještaj o izvršenju) — the schema on which any collection pipeline for this cell must be built. MONSTAT's published 'odluka o izboru' PDF is a concrete example of the older Obrazac-based document format still found on institution sites.

source_name: OTP Group quarterly conference call presentation deck (Montenegro subsidiary slides)
why_relevant: The conference-call deck is the single densest recurring artefact containing Montenegro-level KPIs (profit contribution, NIM, cost/income, risk cost, digital/card metrics commentary) at group-audit quality and within ~6 weeks of quarter end.

source_name: Ziraat Bank Montenegro — e-banking general terms PDF naming Asseco SEE as producer
why_relevant: Bank-published terms-of-use documents routinely name the software producer of the e-banking application (here: Asseco SEE / E-mon Web). Contract and T&C PDFs are an underused, highly reliable vendor-attribution channel where no case study exists.

source_name: Agilcon (Salesforce Platinum partner) — Lovćen Banka portfolio entry
why_relevant: A named vendor portfolio page for a Montenegrin bank (Lovćen Banka), evidencing CRM/Salesforce-side adoption. Confirms the pattern that ME bank procurement surfaces only on the supplier's portfolio page.

source_name: Association of Serbian Banks (UBS-ASB) conference presentations — vendor decks naming bank deployments
why_relevant: Regional banking-association conference proceedings host vendor slide decks (e.g. Halcom ONE cloud-certificate integration into bank digital channels) that disclose architecture and often named deployments. Serbian/regional events regularly cover Montenegrin deployments because vendors serve both markets.

source_name: Banca d'Italia — TIPS / TIPS Clone Western Balkans communications
why_relevant: Operator of the TIPS Clone platform on which Montenegro's instant payments settle. Publishes onboarding windows, participating central banks, technical/governance notes — the upstream roadmap source for ME instant payments.

source_name: CEE Legal Matters — 'SEPA in Montenegro: Benefits and Challenges' (law-firm briefings)
why_relevant: Practitioner analysis dating the ME SEPA sequence (geographic scope Nov 2024, EPC application Apr 2025, adherence Jun 2025, ORD Oct 2025) and flagging legal/compliance frictions for PSPs.

source_name: Council of the EU – Joint Conclusions of the Economic and Financial Dialogue between the EU and the Western Balkans and Türkiye
why_relevant: The ECOFIN-level country-specific policy guidance to Montenegro; the financial-sector recommendations here (e.g. strengthening banking reporting and risk-management frameworks) are agreed commitments that national regulators then translate into law and bylaws.

source_name: European Parliament – rapporteur report on the Commission reports on Montenegro (A10-0093/2025)
why_relevant: Parliamentary scrutiny layer over the Commission's assessment; frequently sharpens or politicises findings on AML, banking supervision independence and financial-sector governance, and signals which reform commitments face EU-side pressure.

source_name: Gecko HRM — Lovćen Banka case study
why_relevant: Named vendor case study on a ME bank (HR/compliance systems). Low strategic value on its own but valuable as a confirmed data point in the vendor-reference index and for mapping the bank's internal digitalisation programme and named executives.

source_name: Lexology — Montenegro payment transactions law commentary
why_relevant: Law-firm commentary on the ME Law on Payment Transactions and its transposition of EU directives (98/26/EC, 2007/64/EC, 2009/44/EC, 2009/110/EC). Explains what licence categories and disclosure duties exist, which is the interpretive key for reading the CBCG registers.

source_name: Mastercard — Montenegro/regional news pages (mastercard.rs Crna Gora subtree)
why_relevant: Mastercard serves Montenegro through the Serbian/regional site in Serbian; this is where ME-specific product launches (Google Pay, tokenisation, issuer partnerships) are announced in local language.

source_name: One Crna Gora (Telekom Austria Group) — data centre / telehousing customer announcements
why_relevant: Joint vendor-customer announcement naming Hipotekarna banka's telehousing/data-centre supplier, quoting the bank's Director of Support, Organisation and Digital Transformation on the selection process. Infrastructure-supplier announcements are a recurring ME channel for procurement disclosure.

source_name: Qualys Customer Success Stories — Crnogorska Komercijalna Banka (CKB) case study
why_relevant: A named, vendor-published case study on Montenegro's largest bank (CKB, OTP Group). Confirms the security-tooling supplier and typically discloses estate size, architecture hints and drivers — exactly the procurement trace ME's private banks never publish themselves.
